insights.claim: MLServer exposes the V2 Inference Protocol over both REST and gRPC on separate ports, with neither transport implementing application-level TLS or authentication.
insights.reasoning: Both the gRPC server (add_insecure_port) and REST server (plain uvicorn) bind without TLS. All encryption and authentication is delegated to the KServe platform layer (kube-rbac-proxy sidecar). This is a deliberate pattern for KServe ServingRuntime containers where the platform owns the security perimeter.

insights.claim: MLServer implements a trusted-runtimes allowlist mechanism that restricts model implementation classes in production mode, enforcing a code execution security boundary at model load time.
insights.reasoning: The trusted-runtimes allowlist at /etc/mlserver/trusted-runtimes.json is baked into the container image at build time. In production mode (file exists), only allowlisted model implementations can be loaded. This prevents arbitrary Python code execution via the model loading API. Import paths are validated against a canonical pattern and built-in aliases normalize legacy paths.

insights.claim: MLServer includes an optional Kafka transport for asynchronous inference, but this capability is not exercised in the standard KServe ServingRuntime deployment.
insights.reasoning: The Kafka server module is present in the codebase with aiokafka as a dependency, but the standard RHOAI deployment uses KServe's synchronous request/response pattern via REST and gRPC. The Kafka transport represents an additional attack surface and dependency that may not be needed in production deployments.
